msg: SixLabors.ImageSharp 3.0.0 and later ships under the Six Labors Split License: a direct reference by a for-profit company with 1M USD or more annual gross revenue needs a commercial licence. Replace with SkiaSharp (MIT): SKBitmap / SKImage.
SixLabors.ImageSharp.Drawing 2.0.0 and later ships under the Six Labors Split License. Replace the drawing calls with SkiaSharp SKCanvas, SKPath and SKPaint.
SixLabors.Fonts 2.0.0 and later ships under the Six Labors Split License. Replace with SkiaSharp SKTypeface / SKFont, and SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz for text shaping.

SixLabors.ImageSharp.Web 3.0.0 and later (and its cache/provider packages) ships under the Six Labors Split License. SkiaSharp has no drop-in middleware: move resizing into your own endpoint that calls SKBitmap.Resize and SKImage.Encode.

Floating or open-ended Six Labors version: NuGet resolves it to the newest release, which is under the Six Labors Split License (ImageSharp 4.x, Fonts 3.x today). Pin an exact version or move to SkiaSharp.

fix: pin below the licence line or move to SkiaSharp
msg: This Six Labors version is still Apache-2.0, but the next major is under the Six Labors Split License. An automated dependency update PR can cross that line; pin it (for example a Dependabot ignore rule) or plan the SkiaSharp move.

System.Drawing.Common 6.0.0 and later is supported on Windows only; on Linux and macOS it throws at run time. This project targets a non-Windows framework. Move to SkiaSharp with SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux.

SkiaSharp is referenced without SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux or SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux.NoDependencies. In a Linux container the native libSkiaSharp is missing and the first SKBitmap call fails with DllNotFoundException.
SkiaSharp native assets version differs from the SkiaSharp package version. SkiaSharp checks the native libSkiaSharp version at load and refuses an incompatible one. Use the same version for both.
Six Labors namespace import. The SkiaSharp equivalent is `using SkiaSharp;`.
ImageSharp Image.Load call. The SkiaSharp equivalent is SKBitmap.Decode(stream) or SKImage.FromEncodedData(data).
ImageSharp Mutate pipeline. In SkiaSharp resize with SKBitmap.Resize(new SKImageInfo(w, h), SKSamplingOptions) and draw on an SKCanvas.
ImageSharp SaveAs call. In SkiaSharp use SKImage.FromBitmap(bmp).Encode(SKEncodedImageFormat.Jpeg, quality) and write the SKData to the stream.
